title: Network Customer Support Engineer
description: Location: Zurich, Paris or Munich Language: Fluency in a two European languages in addition to English. About Us Point One Navigation is building the future of precise location. Our mission is to deliver a unified location platform that enables autonomy, safety, and efficiency across industries from robotics to transportation. We are a high-performance, high-collaboration team that thrives on solving complex problems, moving fast, and delivering impact. Role Outcome The Network Customer Support Engineer owns the customer support experience tied to the reliability, visibility, and operational health of Point One’s correction network. This is a player-coach role. You will personally handle complex technical support cases while also leading the operational systems, monitoring, and processes that ensure the network performs reliably at scale. Success in this role means: Potential customer facing issues are identified and addressed before they impact customers. When incidents do occur, they are resolved quickly with clear communication and strong root-cause analysis. The organization has clear visibility into network health, operational trends, and customer friction. A scalable network operations and support function is built as the company and network footprint grow. Immediate Areas of Focus Own the customer experience of our Network Work with our Network Operations team to understand incidents that affect the customer experience Identify emerging issues and collaborate with engineering and manufacturing teams to understand and support the resolution of those issues. Understand available metrics and dashboards and contribute to the development of these tools to allow for the targeted resolution of customer questions. Deliver High-Quality Technical Support Liaison between Engineering, Network Operations and FAE and FDE team to support the customer. Personally manage high-impact or technically complex support cases. Partner closely with FAEs, Product, and Engineering to diagnose issues and close the loop with customers. Ensure customers receive clear, confident communication during investigations and incidents. Model best-in-class technical troubleshooting and customer engagement practices for the team. Build the Foundation for a Scalable Operations & Support Function Design and implement systems that enable both network operations and customer support to scale. Define a support ticket taxonomy that reflects customer use cases, technical complexity, and operational impact. Support Network Ops team on operational metrics such as: Network uptime and availability Incident response and resolution times Support response and resolution times Alert quality and monitoring coverage Document operational procedures, escalation paths, and ownership models. Develop automation and tooling to reduce manual work and improve operational efficiency. Surface Operational and Customer Insights Identify patterns across support tickets, network events, and operational data. Translate operational signals into actionable insights for Product and Engineering. Ensure recurring issues and infrastructure gaps are clearly surfaced and prioritized. Create lightweight reporting that gives leadership visibility into network reliability, operational trends, and customer friction. Establish Visibility Into Customer Experience Define and implement the right metrics for understanding customer experience and operational impact. Establish mechanisms to collect structured customer feedback without creating noise. Use both operational data and customer feedback to drive continuous improvement. Coach and Develop the Operations & Support Function Act as a player-coach, leading through hands-on operational work while building the foundations of the team. Train and mentor support engineers on troubleshooting methodology, operational awareness, and customer communication. Establish clear expectations for technical depth, ownership, and responsiveness. Continuously raise the operational and support bar as the team grows. Qualifications Fluency in a two European languages in addition to English. Experience in a player-coach technical operations or support role where you owned both hands-on troubleshooting and operational systems. Strong technical background in GPS/GNSS, precise localization, geospatial infrastructure, or closely related domains (robotics, autonomy, embedded systems, positioning technologies). Experience operating or supporting distributed infrastructure or network-based systems. Demonstrated ability to build or significantly improve monitoring, alerting, and operational processes. Proven experience troubleshooting complex technical systems and working directly with customers. Experience conducting incident response and root cause analysis. Ability to define metrics, processes, and documentation without over-engineering. Comfort working cross-functionally with Engineering, Product, and Go-To-Market teams in a fast-moving environment. Bias toward ownership, operational excellence, and continuous improvement. Our Cultural Foundation At Point One, our cultural and operating design is built around one guiding principle: we must move with extreme speed and efficiency of effort to stay in a leadership position. This environment gives people a high level of autonomy and the ability to make a real impact . It also challenges every team member to grow — both professionally and personally. Because we focus on promoting from within rather than relying on external hiring, the opportunities for advancement are tremendous for those who seek them. That said, growth only comes from delivering in the present. What matters most is the job to be done today , not the job you want tomorrow. When we all focus on today’s outcomes with excellence, the path to greater responsibility and growth naturally follows. We think about our culture in two dimensions: How We Show Up Every Day These are the behaviors we expect every team member to bring to work — the foundation of being a consummate, high-output teammate: Trust / Assume Best Intent — Trust allows us to move fast. When we start from trust, we spend no time second-guessing or looking for ulterior motives and thus focus all our energy on acting. High Output, Action Oriented — Our default posture is “yes.” We bias toward action and deliver results quickly, knowing that speed and efficiency compound into impact as we unblock others around us. Divine Discontent — We’re never satisfied with the status quo and are self-motivated to improve ourselves, our work, and our company. We actively seek feedback in real-time to shorten improvement cycles. No Ego, One Team — Collaboration without ego creates leverage. When we win as one team, we eliminate friction and move faster together. raw.description:
Location: Zurich, Paris or Munich

Language: Fluency in a two European languages in addition to English.

About Us

Point One Navigation is building the future of precise location. Our mission is to deliver a unified location platform that enables autonomy, safety, and efficiency across industries from robotics to transportation. We are a high-performance, high-collaboration team that thrives on solving complex problems, moving fast, and delivering impact.

Role Outcome

The Network Customer Support Engineer owns the customer support experience tied to the reliability, visibility, and operational health of Point One’s correction network.

This is a player-coach role. You will personally handle complex technical support cases while also leading the operational systems, monitoring, and processes that ensure the network performs reliably at scale.

Success in this role means:

  • Potential customer facing issues are identified and addressed before they impact customers.

  • When incidents do occur, they are resolved quickly with clear communication and strong root-cause analysis.

  • The organization has clear visibility into network health, operational trends, and customer friction.

  • A scalable network operations and support function is built as the company and network footprint grow.

Immediate Areas of Focus

Own the customer experience of our Network

  • Work with our Network Operations team to understand incidents that affect the customer experience

  • Identify emerging issues and collaborate with engineering and manufacturing teams to understand and support the resolution of those issues.

  • Understand available metrics and dashboards and contribute to the development of these tools to allow for the targeted resolution of customer questions.

Deliver High-Quality Technical Support

  • Liaison between Engineering, Network Operations and FAE and FDE team to support the customer.

  • Personally manage high-impact or technically complex support cases.

  • Partner closely with FAEs, Product, and Engineering to diagnose issues and close the loop with customers.

  • Ensure customers receive clear, confident communication during investigations and incidents.

  • Model best-in-class technical troubleshooting and customer engagement practices for the team.

Build the Foundation for a Scalable Operations & Support Function

  • Design and implement systems that enable both network operations and customer support to scale.

  • Define a support ticket taxonomy that reflects customer use cases, technical complexity, and operational impact.

  • Support Network Ops team on operational metrics such as:

    • Network uptime and availability

    • Incident response and resolution times

    • Support response and resolution times

    • Alert quality and monitoring coverage

    • Document operational procedures, escalation paths, and ownership models.

  • Develop automation and tooling to reduce manual work and improve operational efficiency.

Surface Operational and Customer Insights

  • Identify patterns across support tickets, network events, and operational data.

  • Translate operational signals into actionable insights for Product and Engineering.

  • Ensure recurring issues and infrastructure gaps are clearly surfaced and prioritized.

  • Create lightweight reporting that gives leadership visibility into network reliability, operational trends, and customer friction.

Establish Visibility Into Customer Experience

  • Define and implement the right metrics for understanding customer experience and operational impact.

  • Establish mechanisms to collect structured customer feedback without creating noise.

  • Use both operational data and customer feedback to drive continuous improvement.

Coach and Develop the Operations & Support Function

  • Act as a player-coach, leading through hands-on operational work while building the foundations of the team.

  • Train and mentor support engineers on troubleshooting methodology, operational awareness, and customer communication.

  • Establish clear expectations for technical depth, ownership, and responsiveness.

  • Continuously raise the operational and support bar as the team grows.

Qualifications

  • Fluency in a two European languages in addition to English.

  • Experience in a player-coach technical operations or support role where you owned both hands-on troubleshooting and operational systems.

  • Strong technical background in GPS/GNSS, precise localization, geospatial infrastructure, or closely related domains (robotics, autonomy, embedded systems, positioning technologies).

  • Experience operating or supporting distributed infrastructure or network-based systems.

  • Demonstrated ability to build or significantly improve monitoring, alerting, and operational processes.

  • Proven experience troubleshooting complex technical systems and working directly with customers.

  • Experience conducting incident response and root cause analysis.

  • Ability to define metrics, processes, and documentation without over-engineering.

  • Comfort working cross-functionally with Engineering, Product, and Go-To-Market teams in a fast-moving environment.

  • Bias toward ownership, operational excellence, and continuous improvement.

Our Cultural Foundation

At Point One, our cultural and operating design is built around one guiding principle: we must move with extreme speed and efficiency of effort to stay in a leadership position.

This environment gives people a high level of autonomy and the ability to make a real impact. It also challenges every team member to grow — both professionally and personally. Because we focus on promoting from within rather than relying on external hiring, the opportunities for advancement are tremendous for those who seek them.

That said, growth only comes from delivering in the present. What matters most is the job to be done today, not the job you want tomorrow. When we all focus on today’s outcomes with excellence, the path to greater responsibility and growth naturally follows.

We think about our culture in two dimensions:

How We Show Up Every Day

These are the behaviors we expect every team member to bring to work — the foundation of being a consummate, high-output teammate:

  • Trust / Assume Best Intent — Trust allows us to move fast. When we start from trust, we spend no time second-guessing or looking for ulterior motives and thus focus all our energy on acting.

  • High Output, Action Oriented — Our default posture is “yes.” We bias toward action and deliver results quickly, knowing that speed and efficiency compound into impact as we unblock others around us.

  • Divine Discontent — We’re never satisfied with the status quo and are self-motivated to improve ourselves, our work, and our company. We actively seek feedback in real-time to shorten improvement cycles.

  • No Ego, One Team — Collaboration without ego creates leverage. When we win as one team, we eliminate friction and move faster together.

  • Self Accountability — Taking ownership is the straightest line to learning, self-improvement, and correcting our course of action. And blaming others around us is a fast path to destroying trust.

Operating Principles

These are the systems and norms that amplify speed and efficiency at the company level:

  • Edge Innovation — We bias toward action over approval. Experiment, decide, and move — failure is just a step toward faster learning.

  • No Hierarchies — We practice self-prioritization and go direct to the source. Flattening layers reduces drag and maximizes autonomy.

  • Customer Experience First — We optimize for the end-to-end customer outcome, not functional or departmental efficiency. This focus cuts waste, aligns priorities, and ensures we spend effort where it matters most.

Im März 2026 nahm Rivia in einer Series-A-Finanzierungsrunde 15 Millionen US-Dollar auf, angeführt von Earlybird Venture Capital. Rivia will zur Standardinfrastruktur für die moderne Arzneimittelentwicklung werden und die Durchführung klinischer Studien von Anfang bis Ende grundlegend verändern. Die Rolle Als Senior Talent & People Partner bist du die erste Verstärkung im People-Team von Rivia. Gemeinsam mit der Leitung des People-Bereichs baust du die Funktion von Grund auf auf und entwickelst sie weiter. Du verantwortest den gesamten Recruiting-Prozess und wächst zugleich in weitere People-Themen hinein: Mitarbeitererfahrung, Entwicklung, Performance, Unternehmenskultur, Organisationsgestaltung und Personalprozesse. Die Position bietet erfahrenen Recruiter:innen die Möglichkeit, den nächsten Schritt in eine umfassendere People-Rolle zu machen. Ein fertiges HR-Handbuch, das du einfach übernimmst, gibt es nicht. Gemeinsam entwickeln wir Prozesse, lösen neue Herausforderungen, probieren Ideen aus und schaffen die Grundlagen für das Wachstum von Rivia. Durch praktische Verantwortung, enge Zusammenarbeit und Einblicke in strategische Entscheidungen wie auch operative Herausforderungen lernst du direkt von der Leitung des People-Bereichs. Du bist die enge Sparringspartner:in der Leitung des People-Bereichs: Du denkst selbstständig, arbeitest vertrauensvoll zusammen und packst mit an. Du bringst Ideen ein, hinterfragst Annahmen, handelst schnell und setzt Vorhaben konsequent um. Gesucht ist jemand, der versteht, wie People-Arbeit zum Geschäftserfolg beiträgt, und Führungskräfte wirklich beraten möchte – statt lediglich Prozesse abzuarbeiten. Was dich begeistert Du liebst Recruiting, möchtest dich aber über Talent Acquisition hinaus weiterentwickeln und das gesamte People-Spektrum kennenlernen. Die erste Person im People-Team zu sein und alles von Grund auf mit aufzubauen, reizt dich mehr, als ein bestehendes Handbuch zu pflegen. Du arbeitest eng mit der Leitung des People-Bereichs zusammen, hinterfragst Ideen und lernst durch echte Verantwortung. Du findest außergewöhnliche Talente und baust vertrauensvolle Partnerschaften mit den einstellenden Führungskräften auf. Du löst komplexe Geschäfts- und People-Fragen schnell, neugierig und pragmatisch. Du möchtest die Mitarbeitererfahrung, Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten und Zusammenarbeit verbessern. Du ergreifst die Initiative, behältst verschiedene Prioritäten im Blick und siehst direkt, was deine Arbeit bewirkt. Deine Aufgaben Talent Acquisition Du verantwortest den gesamten Einstellungsprozess über alle Teams hinweg – von der Definition der Rolle über Talent Mapping, Active Sourcing, Interviews und die Betreuung der Kandidat:innen bis hin zu Angeboten und Vertragsabschlüssen. Du berätst einstellende Führungskräfte fundiert zu Recruiting-Strategie, Marktbedingungen, Qualität der Kandidat:innen und möglichen Kompromissen. Du baust proaktiv Talent-Pipelines auf und sorgst für eine wertschätzende, verlässliche Candidate Experience. Du verbesserst Recruiting-Prozesse, ATS-Workflows, Reporting und Recruiting-Analysen. Mitarbeitererfahrung und Entwicklung Gemeinsam mit der Leitung des People-Bereichs entwickelst du Onboarding, Mitarbeitererfahrung, Engagement, Unternehmenskultur und Entwicklungsinitiativen weiter. Du unterstützt die Einführung von Performance Reviews, Feedback-Praktiken, Karriereentwicklung und Angeboten für Führungskräfte. Du hörst den Anliegen von Mitarbeitenden und Führungskräften zu, erkennst Reibungspunkte und setzt Erkenntnisse in konkrete Verbesserungen um. People Operations und Business-Partnerschaft Du hilfst dabei, skalierbare People-Prozesse, Richtlinien, Systeme und Abläufe entlang des gesamten Beschäftigungsverhältnisses von Grund auf aufzubauen. Du unterstützt Führungskräfte mit pragmatischer, geschäftsorientierter Beratung und durchdachten Personalentscheidungen. Mit wachsendem Verantwortungsbereich arbeitest du an Projekten zu Organisationsgestaltung, Vergütung, HR Operations und People Analytics mit. Du erkennst Probleme früh, schlägst Lösungen vor und kümmerst dich um deren Umsetzung, statt auf Anweisungen zu warten. Was du mitbringst Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse. Umfassende Erfahrung im Recruiting über den gesamten Einstellungsprozess hinweg sowie nachweisbare Erfolge bei der eigenständigen Besetzung anspruchsvoller Positionen. Den Wunsch, dich in eine umfassendere People-Rolle weiterzuentwickeln; Erfahrung als HR-Generalist:in ist nicht erforderlich. Du baust gern Neues auf, löst Probleme, handelst schnell, denkst kritisch und übernimmst Verantwortung bis zur Umsetzung. Geschäftssinn und die Sicherheit, einstellende Führungskräfte und andere Verantwortliche zu hinterfragen, zu überzeugen und zu beraten. Du fühlst dich wohl mit offenen Fragestellungen, hohen Erwartungen, mehreren parallelen Prioritäten und praktischer Arbeit. Ausgeprägte Kommunikationsfähigkeit, gutes Urteilsvermögen, Organisationstalent und Erfahrung im Stakeholder-Management. Neugier, Bescheidenheit und die Bereitschaft, neue People-Fachgebiete zu erschließen. Von Vorteil Kenntnisse des Schweizer Arbeitsrechts. Einblicke in Mitarbeiterentwicklung, Performance Management oder Mitarbeiterengagement. Erfahrung in einem Startup oder Scale-up sowie Vertrautheit mit ATS-, HRIS- oder People-Analytics-Systemen. Bewerbungsprozess Unser Bewerbungsprozess dauert in der Regel zwei bis vier Wochen und umfasst vier Schritte: Kennenlernen: 30-minütiges erstes Gespräch mit dem People-Team. Vertiefendes Gespräch: Austausch mit der Leitung des People-Bereichs über Recruiting, Business-Partnerschaft und deine Entwicklungsziele. Praxisaufgabe: Gemeinsame Bearbeitung einer realistischen Recruiting- und People-Herausforderung. Kennenlernen des Teams: Gespräche vor Ort in Zürich, um herauszufinden, ob wir gut zueinander passen. Unsere Werte Bei Rivia setzen wir auf Spitzenleistung, kontinuierliches Lernen und den Erfolg unserer Kund:innen und unseres Teams. Mit vollem Einsatz gewinnen: Herausforderungen mit Entschlossenheit, Ausdauer und Tatkraft angehen. Veränderung annehmen: Wandel als Chance zur Verbesserung sehen. Warum eigentlich nicht?: Annahmen hinterfragen und neugierig bleiben. Lücken erkennen: Probleme frühzeitig identifizieren und lösen. Gemeinsam Verantwortung übernehmen: Zusammen für Ergebnisse einstehen und einander unterstützen. Lösungen mit Mehrwert schaffen: Sinnvolle Ergebnisse erzielen, die wirklich etwas bewirken. Deine Aufgaben

Talent Acquisition

  • Du verantwortest den gesamten Einstellungsprozess über alle Teams hinweg – von der Definition der Rolle über Talent Mapping, Active Sourcing, Interviews und die Betreuung der Kandidat:innen bis hin zu Angeboten und Vertragsabschlüssen.

  • Gemeinsam mit der Leitung des People-Bereichs entwickelst du Onboarding, Mitarbeitererfahrung, Engagement, Unternehmenskultur und Entwicklungsinitiativen weiter.

People Operations und Business-Partnerschaft

  • Du hilfst dabei, skalierbare People-Prozesse, Richtlinien, Systeme und Abläufe entlang des gesamten Beschäftigungsverhältnisses von Grund auf aufzubauen.

Bewerbungsprozess

raw.description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times.

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies.

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

About the role

BLP only works when it talks to our customers’ ERP systems. As an Integration Engineer, you build and own those connections and keep live integrations running for enterprise customers. Every new ERP system is a new problem to solve. You’ll lead our Oracle integrations across Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite and JD Edwards, while also contributing to other integrations.

 

What you’ll do

  • Own our integrations with Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite and JD Edwards and ensure their market fit, usability and reliability.

  • Design and implement interfaces for diverse protocols: REST, SOAP, direct DB access and file transfers.

  • Explore new ERP systems and determine the best way to connect them.

  • Build new ERP integrations, often in close collaboration with pilot customers.

  • Own existing integrations end to end, including issue resolution, and document them so teammates can pick them up.

  • Enable technical project managers to consult on, install and configure mature integrations.

 

What you'll bring

  • Hands-on integration experience with Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite or JD Edwards EnterpriseOne, ideally more than one. You have built or maintained interfaces yourself, not only used the system as a functional consultant or key user.

  • Experience with the native interfaces of at least one of these:

    • Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP: REST and SOAP web services, File-Based Data Import (FBDI) through the ERP Integration Service, and data extraction with BI Publisher or BI Cloud Connector (BICC).

    • NetSuite: SuiteTalk REST and SOAP web services, SuiteQL, SuiteScript 2.x (e.g., RESTlets, Map/Reduce scripts), and Token-Based Authentication or OAuth 2.0.

    • JD Edwards EnterpriseOne: AIS Server and Orchestrator, Business Services (BSSV), and Z-file interface tables (e.g., F0411Z1) with their batch processors.

  • A good understanding of purchase-to-pay data in Oracle ERPs: suppliers, purchase orders, receipts and supplier invoice matching.

  • Solid programming skills in at least one backend language. We build our integrations in Go. If you come from Java, C#, Python or similar and are keen to pick up Go, that works for us.

  • A degree in computer science or a related field, or equivalent experience.

  • A structured, self-reliant way of working, and ideally experience in a client-facing role.

  • Fluent English. German is a plus, as most of our customers are in the DACH region.

Nice to have:

  • Experience with both cloud (Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite) and on-premise (JD Edwards) environments, and the constraints of each (e.g., no direct database access in Fusion, governance limits in NetSuite).

  • Extensive experience with SQL, common data formats (JSON, XML, CSV) and transports (REST/SOAP APIs, SFTP).

  • Familiarity with modern engineering practices: Git, code reviews, automated testing and CI/CD.

  • Integration experience with other ERPs, such as SAP, Microsoft Dynamics or Infor.

 

Integration Engineer or Senior Integration Engineer

We hire at both levels. Four things decide where you start: years of experience, breadth of experience, coaching experience and scope.

Integration Engineer

  • Years: 2+ years of hands-on integration work, including Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite or JD Edwards.

  • Breadth: in-depth experience with one Oracle ERP and its interfaces.

  • Coaching: you learn quickly from senior colleagues and share what you learn with the team.

  • Scope: you deliver and maintain integrations and resolve issues independently, with guidance on architecture decisions.

Senior Integration Engineer

  • Years: 5+ years of hands-on integration work, several of them with Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, NetSuite or JD Edwards.

  • Breadth: integration experience across two or more of Fusion, NetSuite and JD Edwards, or across Oracle and other ERPs, in cloud and on-premise environments.

  • Coaching: you have coached or mentored other engineers and help technical project managers grow.

  • Scope: you own our Oracle integrations end to end, set technical direction and take on the most complex customer cases.

Why BLP

  • Real impact: your integrations decide whether a customer goes live.

  • Breadth: Oracle, Infor, Microsoft Dynamics and many other ERPs, plus EDI and e-invoicing standards.

  • Growth: fast-tracked growth, with promotions and a bonus scheme that includes company shares.

  • Team: regular team events.

Practical information

  • Location: our Zurich office, hybrid with 3+ office days per week, or remotely from anywhere in Europe.

  • If you work remotely, we pay for regular visits and stays in Zurich.

  • Employment: full-time, permanent.

 

Learn more about blp and our values at blp.digital/company/careers.

title: Senior Control Systems Engineer
description: Fusionality is building the measurement, simulation and control stack of the fusion energy reactors of the future. Our technology enables effective and reliable operation, monitoring, and analysis of high-temperature plasmas in fusion devices — which will one day provide clean, practically limitless power to the grid. We have spun out of EPFL’s Swiss Plasma Center and have just completed our pre-seed fundraise. We are looking for a Senior Control Systems Engineer to join our founding team in Lausanne and help build our core technology. This job is for you if you are a passionate engineer with deep knowledge cutting across real-time / embedded systems, software and hardware, and excited about building the systems to monitor and control real-world fusion plasmas. Tasks Implement real-time control, analysis, data acquisition systems in the kHz to MHz range, as individual contributor and in a team. Integrate solutions across a variety of company products and services as well as on our in-house test beds. Provide technical leadership within a growing real-time control and software engineering team that you will help to build. Translate customer needs into requirements and specifications. Requirements Experience taking hard-real-time acquisition and control loops from incomplete requirements through to commissioning on hardware, in domains such as automotive, robotics, embedded, electrical and/or scientific instrumentation. ‘Full stack’: familiarity with all aspects of real-time technologies, from physical/DAQ, real-time software frameworks and middleware, real-time OS and integration. Fluency in a mix of high-level and low-level languages such as C, C++, Rust, MATLAB/Simulink, Python. Obsession with code quality, testing and reliability. Experience with distributed real-time systems, real-time networking and field buses and/or SCADA is an advantage. Experience with embedded/μC/FPGA technologies and/or safety critical systems is an advantage. Benefits The unique opportunity to play a foundational role at a dynamic, fast-growing startup, shaping the technical solutions and products from the ground up. The opportunity to build cutting edge technology to monitor and control plasmas in real fusion devices, working side-by-side with leading plasma and control experts. Great working conditions, located in Lausanne, Switzerland, a city and country known for its high quality of life. Competitive salary and equity compensation and benefits including immigration assistance. If you are excited about joining our team, send your CV including information about a real-time system you have taken into operation. We're looking forward to hearing from you. Corporate governance and administration

  • Coordinate Board and shareholder matters with the CEO and legal counsel, including meeting preparation, resolutions, corporate records and follow through on decisions.

  • Maintain a clear overview of the company’s corporate structure, shareholder arrangements, financing agreements and material contractual commitments.

  • Track related obligations and deadlines, ensuring clear ownership and timely action across relevant functions.

  • Ensure governance requirements, delegated authorities and approval processes are understood and applied.

  • Manage relationships with external legal advisers, insurers and corporate service providers.

Policies, compliance and internal controls

  • Coordinate the development, implementation and review of company policies in line with business needs, investor commitments and applicable requirements.

  • Coordinate communication and training, maintaining appropriate records.

  • Monitor implementation, address gaps with relevant owners and bring matters requiring attention to the leadership team.

Swiss site and corporate services

  • Coordinate Swiss site administration and corporate support activities, working closely with production, engineering and other teams.

  • Oversee facilities, workplace services and external providers, ensuring a safe and effective working environment.

  • Help resolve site issues and coordinate improvements that support daily operations.

  • Oversee IT services and infrastructure through internal resources and external partners.

  • Drive improvements in digital tools, systems and administrative processes.

  • Coordinate site procedures and business continuity arrangements with relevant specialists.

HR oversight and organisational support

  • Oversee the HR function, supporting the HR team in delivering effective people processes and reliable daily operations.

  • Work with the CEO and managers on workforce planning, organisational changes and recruitment priorities.

  • Ensure employment administration, payroll coordination and HR policies are managed consistently and appropriately.

  • Support clear internal communication and effective collaboration across teams.

Financial management and business support

  • Oversee budgeting, forecasting, cash flow planning and financial reporting, supported by internal finance resources and external partners.

  • Ensure reliable accounting, statutory reporting, tax and audit processes.

  • Provide clear financial visibility to support business decisions and resource allocation.

  • Maintain appropriate financial controls, spending discipline and approval processes.

  • Monitor costs and commitments with budget owners and programme teams.

  • Support investor reporting, financing activities and due diligence when required.

Leadership and continuous improvement

  • Lead and support a small multidisciplinary team, coordinating external expertise where needed.

  • Set priorities, allocate resources and ensure actions are completed.

  • Build trusted working relationships with managers and colleagues across the organisation.

  • Simplify processes and adapt corporate services as the business evolves.

Your profile

  • Experience in a broad finance and administration, corporate services or business operations leadership role.

  • Strong understanding of corporate governance and confidence working with corporate documents, contractual commitments and legal advisers.

  • Experience implementing policies and translating compliance requirements into practical ways of working.

  • Experience coordinating site operations or corporate support functions, ideally in a technology or industrial environment.

  • Familiarity with the Swiss business environment and relevant administrative and statutory requirements.

  • Ability to lead across different functions, drawing on the expertise of colleagues and external partners.

  • Sound judgement, discretion and the ability to build trust with people across the organisation.

  • A practical, collaborative approach, with strong organisational skills and a willingness to get involved in day to day matters.

  • Fluent English and French.

  • A relevant qualification in finance, business administration or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

At H55, you will work closely with the people developing electric aviation technology and help create the conditions for them to succeed. Your decisions will shape how we work, support our teams and move the business forward.

title: Scientific Account Executive
description: Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments. We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world. We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today. Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development. We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation. About the role This is a hybrid sales and customer success role for someone with real scientific depth. You'll be the primary point of contact for customers — from first conversation through ongoing engagement. That means understanding what a protein design team is actually trying to achieve, helping them pick the right assays, making sure their experiments are set up correctly, and translating results back into language that's useful for their programs. The day-to-day: Running technical sales calls where you discuss binding kinetics, expression systems, and assay design, not just pricing Onboarding new customers and helping them design their first experiments on the platform Monitoring ongoing accounts, flagging issues early, and proactively suggesting next steps based on their results Working with the biology team to troubleshoot when a customer's experiment doesn't go as expected Identifying expansion opportunities within existing accounts — new targets, new assay types, larger campaigns You won't be handed a script. You'll need to understand the science well enough to earn trust from PhD-level protein engineers and CSOs, while also being commercially sharp enough to close deals and grow accounts. Responsibilities Own the full customer lifecycle: prospecting, technical sales conversations, deal closing, onboarding, and ongoing account management. Serve as the technical point of contact for customers. Understand their protein engineering goals and recommend the right experiments (binding, expression, thermostability, enzyme activity). Understand and explain our assay capabilities in depth: BLI, SPR, cell-free expression, and emerging assay types. Know when each is appropriate and what the data means. Work closely with the biology team to ensure experiments are designed correctly and results are communicated clearly. Build and maintain a pipeline of commercial opportunities across customer segments: AI-driven protein design companies, biotech startups, pharma R&D teams, and academic labs. Develop proposals and quotes tailored to customer needs, from small pilot experiments to large-scale data generation campaigns. Represent Adaptyv at conferences and industry events. Be able to have deep technical conversations at the booth, not just hand out brochures. Feed customer insights back to the product and biology teams: what assays are people asking for, what's missing, where are we losing deals. What we're looking for Scientific background in protein engineering, biochemistry, biophysics, or a related field. You should be comfortable discussing binding kinetics (KD, kon, koff), expression systems, and assay design without needing to look things up. Connect experimental results back to the protein side — sequence, structure, and design — so wet-lab data and computational models reinforce each other. Turn foundry output into structured, documented, benchmark-grade datasets that are a genuine asset for our customers and for training and evaluating protein-design models. We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation. About the Role Our lab produces binding data faster than any one person can look at it. Runs come off the Gators and the Carterra, go through our processing pipeline, and land in a review queue. Somebody with real judgment then has to decide: is this curve real? Is that a fit artifact or a genuine two-state binding event? Does this replicate get delivered, or does the sample get re-run? That person is you. The second half of the job is talking to the customer about it. When a design team gets a plate back and three of their best predictions look like non-binders, they want to talk to someone who can explain why: reference subtraction, avidity, an off-rate at the edge of what the instrument resolves, or simply a bad protein. You'll be that person, on the call, sharing your screen, walking through sensorgrams. This is a role for a scientist who is very good at kinetics and also likes people. If you like one but not the other, you'll be unhappy here. What You'll Do Review the binding data coming out of the lab. Every SPR and BLI run passes through our processing pipeline and then to human review, and you're the expert eye on the output. You decide what gets delivered, what gets flagged, and what gets re-run. Judge the curves, not just the numbers. A clean-looking Kd on a bad fit is worse than no number at all. You know the difference between a real off-rate and a drifting baseline, and you can say why. Review data from our other assays too: thermostability, expression, developability, enzyme activity. Binding is the core of the role but it isn't all of it. Talk to customers about their results. Deliverable walkthroughs, follow-up questions, and the awkward conversation when the data doesn't say what they hoped. You explain what we measured, how confident we are, and what to do next. Turn review into experimental design. When something needs a re-run, you decide what changes: orientation, regeneration, concentration series, or a switch from BLI to SPR for the sensitivity. Analyze at the batch level, not just the sample level. With hundreds of results per experiment, you should be writing a script to find the pattern rather than clicking through a queue. Systematic drift, a bad reference channel, or a target lot behaving differently than the last one shows up in aggregate long before it shows up in any single curve. Feed what you learn back into the pipeline. When you catch a case where automation passed something it shouldn't have, or failed something it shouldn't have, that becomes a concrete requirement for the software team. Work closely with production (what actually happened in the lab), QC (systematic quality), and customer success (the relationship around the science). What We're Looking For MSc / PhD in biochemistry, biophysics, or a relevant field, plus 3+ years working hands-on with binding kinetics. Deep SPR and BLI experience. Biacore, Carterra, Octet, Gator: the platform matters less than the fact that you've run these assays, troubleshot them, and interpreted a lot of data from them. You've seen enough sensorgrams to know immediately when one is lying to you. Real fitting judgment. 1:1 vs. bivalent, when steady-state is appropriate and when it isn't, how mass transport and avidity distort a result. You can defend a Kd, or refuse to report one. Strong data analysis skills. Python or R, enough to pull a few hundred results out of a database, fit them, plot them, and find the outliers. This role generates too much data to review by hand. You use AI tools seriously. We run on Claude Code and similar tooling internally, and the people who get the most done here are the ones who reach for it by default: writing the analysis script, querying the database, building the one-off dashboard. You don't need to have done this before, but you need to want to. If your instinct is that real scientists do it by hand, this isn't the place. A self-starter who works independently. Nobody is going to hand you a prioritized queue every morning. You'll figure out what matters most, go do it, and tell us what you found. A fast learner. Our platform, our assays, and our software change constantly. You'll be handed unfamiliar tools and expected to be productive with them quickly. Startup speed, not academic pace. Experiments ship to paying customers on deadlines. Getting a good answer this week beats a perfect one next quarter, and we'd rather flag an ambiguous result than sit on it. About the Role

Our lab produces binding data faster than any one person can look at it. Runs come off the Gators and the Carterra, go through our processing pipeline, and land in a review queue. Somebody with real judgment then has to decide: is this curve real? Is that a fit artifact or a genuine two-state binding event? Does this replicate get delivered, or does the sample get re-run? That person is you.

The second half of the job is talking to the customer about it. When a design team gets a plate back and three of their best predictions look like non-binders, they want to talk to someone who can explain why: reference subtraction, avidity, an off-rate at the edge of what the instrument resolves, or simply a bad protein. You'll be that person, on the call, sharing your screen, walking through sensorgrams.

This is a role for a scientist who is very good at kinetics and also likes people. If you like one but not the other, you'll be unhappy here.

What You'll Do

  • Review the binding data coming out of the lab. Every SPR and BLI run passes through our processing pipeline and then to human review, and you're the expert eye on the output. You decide what gets delivered, what gets flagged, and what gets re-run.

  • Judge the curves, not just the numbers. A clean-looking Kd on a bad fit is worse than no number at all. You know the difference between a real off-rate and a drifting baseline, and you can say why.

  • Review data from our other assays too: thermostability, expression, developability, enzyme activity. Binding is the core of the role but it isn't all of it.

  • Talk to customers about their results. Deliverable walkthroughs, follow-up questions, and the awkward conversation when the data doesn't say what they hoped. You explain what we measured, how confident we are, and what to do next.

  • Turn review into experimental design. When something needs a re-run, you decide what changes: orientation, regeneration, concentration series, or a switch from BLI to SPR for the sensitivity.

  • Analyze at the batch level, not just the sample level. With hundreds of results per experiment, you should be writing a script to find the pattern rather than clicking through a queue. Systematic drift, a bad reference channel, or a target lot behaving differently than the last one shows up in aggregate long before it shows up in any single curve.

  • Feed what you learn back into the pipeline. When you catch a case where automation passed something it shouldn't have, or failed something it shouldn't have, that becomes a concrete requirement for the software team.

  • Work closely with production (what actually happened in the lab), QC (systematic quality), and customer success (the relationship around the science).

What We're Looking For

  • MSc / PhD in biochemistry, biophysics, or a relevant field, plus 3+ years working hands-on with binding kinetics.

  • Deep SPR and BLI experience. Biacore, Carterra, Octet, Gator: the platform matters less than the fact that you've run these assays, troubleshot them, and interpreted a lot of data from them. You've seen enough sensorgrams to know immediately when one is lying to you.

  • Real fitting judgment. 1:1 vs. bivalent, when steady-state is appropriate and when it isn't, how mass transport and avidity distort a result. You can defend a Kd, or refuse to report one.

  • Strong data analysis skills. Python or R, enough to pull a few hundred results out of a database, fit them, plot them, and find the outliers. This role generates too much data to review by hand.

  • You use AI tools seriously. You don't need to have done this before, but you need to want to. If your instinct is that real scientists do it by hand, this isn't the place.

  • A self-starter who works independently. Nobody is going to hand you a prioritized queue every morning. You'll figure out what matters most, go do it, and tell us what you found.

  • A fast learner. Our platform, our assays, and our software change constantly. You'll be handed unfamiliar tools and expected to be productive with them quickly.

About myTomorrows 

myTomorrows is a global health tech company dedicated to breaking down barriers for patients seeking treatment options.   

We strive to enable earlier and better treatment access by bridging the gap between those searching for possible options, and the companies who develop them. We work closely with patients, healthcare professionals, trial sites, patient advocacy groups, and BioPharma – connecting key stakeholders in the drug development ecosystem.   

We’ve developed a cutting-edge AI-powered technology platform that simplifies and streamlines access to drugs in development. To support our users and clients, we have a range of industry-expert specialized teams ready to help. Our services include clinical trial patient recruitment, Expanded Access Program management and Real-World Data collection.   

With a global footprint spanning 134 countries, to date we’ve supported over 17,000 patients, 3,000 physicians and 350 sites, earning the trust of 60+ BioPharma companies. In October 2025, we closed a €25M investment with Avego Healthcare Capital to fuel our global ambitions and scale the business.  

Join us in shaping the future of treatment access - making tomorrow’s therapies accessible for people who need them today. 

The opportunity: Full Stack Engineer

As a Full Stack Engineer, you will take primary ownership of our frontend experience while being capable of making the backend changes needed to unblock yourself and your team. You'll work closely with Backend Engineers, DevOps Engineers, and stakeholders to deliver scalable, reliable, and high-performance products end-to-end, from pixel to API.

Given that most of our team is located in the Netherlands, we only consider candidates for this position who live within commuting distance of our office in Amsterdam.

What you'll do in this role

  • Design, develop, and maintain frontend components in Angular (and Lit HTML where applicable), ensuring optimal performance, responsiveness, and usability.

  • Own the integration layer between frontend and backend: consume and contribute to OpenAPI-defined APIs, handle data contracts, and wire up microservices cleanly.

  • Make targeted backend changes, new endpoints, tweaks to existing services, minor data model updates, so you can ship features without always depending on a dedicated backend engineer.

  • Contribute to architectural discussions across the full stack, from UI component structure to API design and data access patterns.

  • Participate actively in code reviews, providing feedback on both frontend and backend code quality, adherence to standards, and performance.

  • Mentor and support junior engineers across the stack.

  • Stay current with evolving frontend and full-stack best practices.

What you bring to the table

  • 3+ years of experience in frontend or full stack engineering.

  • Strong proficiency in Angular and experience with component-based frameworks such as Lit HTML.

  • Solid understanding of responsive design, UX/UI principles, and a keen eye for design detail.

  • Proven experience integrating with APIs and microservices, you understand HTTP, REST conventions, auth flows, and error handling deeply.

  • Working proficiency in Python, enough to navigate a FastAPI codebase, add or adjust endpoints, and write Pydantic models and SQLAlchemy queries.

  • Familiarity with relational databases (MySQL/PostgreSQL) at the query and schema level.

  • Experience with containerised workflows using Docker.

  • Excellent problem-solving skills; comfortable working independently and collaboratively.

  • Strong English communication skills and ability to work across disciplines.

  • Comfortable using AI-assisted development tools (e.g. Claude Code, Cursor, or similar) as part of daily workflow.

  • Familiarity with LLM API integration (OpenAI, Anthropic, or similar) and an understanding of the UX patterns specific to AI-powered features.

What success in the first 6 months looks like

  • You've built trust with Backend, DevOps, and Product peers and taken clear ownership of 2–3 frontend domains, including their design system consistency and API integration contracts.

  • You've delivered frontend features end-to-end, from UX design discussion through Angular implementation, API wiring, tests, and documentation, without needing hand-holding at either layer.

  • You've unblocked yourself (and others) by making safe, well-reviewed backend changes: adding an endpoint, adjusting a response model, or optimising a query, rather than waiting in a queue.

  • You've raised frontend quality: responsive across devices, accessible, consistent with our design system, and validated against real API contracts rather than mocks.

  • You've contributed to meaningful observability on the frontend, error tracking, performance budgets, and linked them to backend SLIs where relevant.

  • You've shared knowledge through documentation, code reviews, and mentoring, so the team's frontend capability grows with you.

Current tech stack

We're fully cloud-native on AWS, with a lean, API-first product development approach.

Frontend: Angular · Lit HTML · Headless Wagtail · WordPress

Backend: Python · FastAPI · Pydantic · SQLAlchemy · MySQL · Neo4j

Platform: AWS · Kubernetes · Terraform · Docker · GitHub Actions · ruff · UV · pre-commit · Renovate

Our platform runs on Kubernetes-managed services and Terraform for infrastructure as code. We continue expanding capabilities in knowledge graphs (Neo4j) and modern data access patterns.

What we offer:

  • Impactful work that helps patients gain access to potentially lifesaving treatments. 

  • International work environment, scale-up energy and a flat organizational structure that encourages creativity and accountability. 

  • Competitive salary, annual performance bonus and an Employee Stock Option Plan. 

  • Great career development opportunities in a fast-growing company.  

  • Learning and development budget alongside internal knowledge sharing sessions. 

  • Attractive pension plan, full premium covered by myTomorrows. 

  • Hybrid working model. 

  • Policies to support working parents. 

  • Healthy lunch at the thriving Amsterdam office.  

  • Unlimited access to professional guidance by certified psychologists via OpenUp  

  • Enjoy monthly events hosted by our vibrant Culture Club as well as an annual ‘myTomorrowland’ company-wide celebration! 

Equal opportunities

myTomorrows is an Equal Opportunity Employer and, beyond upholding discrimination-free practices, we are committed to cultivating a workplace where difference and diversity are protected and celebrated. The best work comes from our best selves, and we go to great lengths in supporting our team members to be just that.

title: Social Creative stage
description: Als stagiair Social Creative heb je een schermtijd die je liever niet hardop zegt en ben je altijd op de hoogte van de laatste social media trends. Van feta-ovenpasta tot knapperige aardappelsalade en van chopped sandwich tot de omelet uit The Bear - jij was er allemaal als eerste bij. Je maakt foto’s en short-form video’s waar menig maag van gaat rommelen en je weet deze beelden tot hapklare content te maken. Kom jij ons gezellige social team per februari 2027 versterken voor een half jaar? Wat je gaat doen Je bent als eerste op de hoogte van de nieuwste foodtrends en komt met originele ideeën om hierop in te haken op een manier die past bij Crisp. Daarbij krijg je veel vrijheid om je eigen creativiteit in te zetten. Je weet welke ingrediënten er nodig zijn om de lekkerste foto’s en video’s te maken en kunt deze beelden zelf bewerken tot smaakmakende content. Met je handen uit de mouwen mentaliteit ondersteun je ons social team bij het coördineren van foto en videoshoots. Je zit niet elke dag achter je laptop, maar gaat ook regelmatig op pad, bijvoorbeeld om leveranciers te ontmoeten of content te schieten op locatie. Je helpt bij het beheren van de social media kanalen van Crisp. Je houdt de planning bij, zorgt dat alles op rolletjes loopt en draagt bij aan een dynamische, leuke rol binnen een gezellig team. Dit ben jij Je zit vol ideeën om onze socials naar een next level te tillen Je verslindt alle vormen van digitale content en Instagram en TikTok kennen geen geheimen voor jou. Je hebt een flexibele werkhouding. Een plotselinge update van Instagram brengt jou niet van je stuk. Je bent creatief en proactief. Je werkt graag zelfstandig, maar sparren met het social team vind je net zo leuk. Je beheerst de Nederlandse taal uitstekend, zowel mondeling als in schrift. Je bent 32-40 uur per week beschikbaar voor minimaal 5 maanden. Wat wij bieden Werken bij een B Corp gecertificeerd bedrijf, waarbij je de kans krijgt om je stempel te drukken op ons voedselsysteem en échte verandering teweeg te brengen. Enthousiaste en ondernemende collega’s om mee te werken en te leren. Een kijkje in de keuken van een van de snelst ontwikkelende bedrijven in de Europese markt. Een gratis lunch van Crisp. Elke maand food for thought, met workshops en talks via de Crisp University. Tijd om je collega’s te leren kennen tijdens sport, events en proeverijen. Aandacht voor je mentale gezondheid met online begeleiding van erkende psychologen via OpenUp. En... fikse korting op je Crisp boodschappen, omdat je thuis natuurlijk ook goed wilt eten. Onze selectieprocedure Solliciteer via onderstaande button. Hoe meer je kunt delen over jezelf en de reden dat je solliciteert, hoe beter. Bij Crisp streven we naar een inclusieve en diverse werkomgeving waarin iedereen welkom is, ongeacht hun achtergrond, geslacht, leeftijd, etniciteit, seksuele geaardheid, religie of beperking. Wij moedigen sollicitanten met diverse perspectieven en achtergronden aan om te solliciteren en geloven in gelijke kansen voor iedereen. We waarderen de unieke bijdragen die elke medewerker kan leveren en zijn vastbesloten om een inclusieve werkplek te creëren waarin iedereen wordt gerespecteerd en gewaardeerd. title: Reliability & Maintenance Engineer | DSL-01
description: Please note: For this role proficiency in both Dutch and English is required. Reliability & Maintenance Engineer | DSL-01 As Reliability & Maintenance Engineer DSL-01, you are responsible for building and continuously improving the facility's maintenance, reliability, and asset integrity framework. Reporting to the Engineering Manager, you help ensure the plant operates safely, reliably, and efficiently. The role starts with a strong Maintenance Engineering focus. Your priority will be to help establish the maintenance and reliability foundation of DSL-01 by answering a fundamental question: "how do we maintain our assets safely, reliably, and efficiently throughout their lifecycle?" You will translate reliability studies, equipment criticality assessments, and integrity requirements into practical maintenance plans, inspection programmes, spare parts strategies, and asset management processes. As the facility moves into stable operations, the focus gradually shifts towards Reliability Engineering, where you will use asset health monitoring, root cause analysis, and continuous improvement to prevent failures and improve long-term asset performance. Working closely with operations, maintenance, engineering, and external specialists, you will help reduce technical risk and improve asset reliability from day one. You will: Develop and continuously improve maintenance, inspection, and asset integrity strategies Translate reliability studies, FMECA analyses, and engineering data into practical maintenance plans within the CMMS/EAM system Act as owner of the asset register from a maintenance, reliability, and integrity perspective Support the implementation and continuous development of the facility's CMMS/EAM system Drive reliability improvements through asset health monitoring, KPI analysis, and predictive maintenance techniques Lead Root Cause Analyses (RCA) and implement sustainable corrective actions Monitor and improve reliability performance indicators such as MTBF, MTTR, availability, and inspection compliance Support asset improvement, modification, and long-term replacement strategies throughout the asset lifecycle Your profile As a growing company in a rapidly evolving industry, we are looking for people who embrace change and are motivated to actively contribute to building and scaling our business. You are someone who feels comfortable in an entrepreneurial environment, takes ownership, and enjoys turning complex technical challenges into practical solutions. You recognize yourself in the following: Must have Fluent in Dutch and English Bachelor's degree in a relevant engineering discipline (i.e. electrical or mechanical) 5+ years of experience in Reliability Engineering, Maintenance Engineering, Asset Integrity, or Asset Management Experience with RCM, FMEA/FMECA, RCA, and maintenance strategy development Experience with CMMS/EAM systems such as SAP PM, Maximo, or IFS Preferred Experience in chemical, petrochemical, energy, or other process industries like food or FMCG Experience with CMMS/EAM implementation or optimisation Experience with predictive maintenance and condition monitoring Knowledge of ATEX, PED, and asset integrity management About DSL-01 DSL-01 is SkyNRG’s frontrunning renewable fuels facility in Delfzijl, Netherlands. The plant will produce Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) from residual fats and greases using the HEFA (Hydrotreated Esters and Fatty Acids) pathway, with additional renewable products like butane, propane, and naphtha as by-products. DSL-01 is the first facility in Europe dedicated entirely to SAF and its by-products. Once operational, it will produce 100,000 tonnes of SAF and 35,000 tonnes of sustainable by-products per year, cutting greenhouse gas emissions by around 80% compared to conventional jet fuel. Construction started in 2026, with first fuel expected in 2028. The project includes the main facility, pipelines, and temporary work areas. At DSL-01, you will be part of a team building a state-of-the-art industrial plant from the ground up, contributing to a truly sustainable energy future. Environmental and social responsibility are at the heart of DSL-01. We follow international frameworks and Dutch regulations to manage impacts on people, nature, and local communities. We are committed to offering an attractive total package to ensure we attract the best talent in the market. This includes a competitive salary, performance-based incentives, and a range of benefits that support your personal and professional growth. Is this you? At DSL-01, you will work in a dynamic, innovative environment where technical curiosity, problem-solving, and teamwork are valued. You will engage with operators, engineers, and managers across disciplines, helping to bring a pioneering renewable fuels facility to life while making a real impact on the planet. Your profile

As a growing company in a rapidly evolving industry, we are looking for people who embrace change and are motivated to actively contribute to building and scaling our business. You recognize yourself in the following:

Must have

  • Je hebt minimaal 5 jaar ervaring binnen Health, Safety, Environment of QHSES-gerelateerde functies.

  • Je hebt ervaring in een industriële, chemische, productie-, energie- of andere hoog-risico omgeving.

  • Je hebt een goed begrip van arbeidsveiligheidswetgeving, risicomanagement en compliance vereisten.

  • Je hebt ervaring met ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 45001 en/of Seveso/BRZO-gerelateerde kaders.

  • Je bent bekend met risicogestuurd werken en continu verbeteren.

Bonus

  • Certificeringen zoals NEBOSH, HVK, MVK of vergelijkbaar.

  • Ervaring met chemische veiligheidsvraagstukken en REACH-verplichtingen.

  • Ervaring met ISO-certificeringstrajecten en externe audits.

  • Ervaring binnen greenfield-projecten of grootschalige industriële bouw- en opstartprojecten.

Over DSL-01

In Delfzijl bouwen we aan DSL-01, een fabriek van SkyNRG voor hernieuwbare brandstoffen. Hier produceren we Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) uit reststromen zoals gebruikte vetten en oliën, met HEFA-technologie. Daarnaast maken we bijproducten zoals butaan, propaan en nafta.

DSL-01 wordt de eerste fabriek in Europa die volledig gericht is op SAF en bijbehorende duurzame bijproducten. Als de fabriek in bedrijf is, produceren we jaarlijks 100.000 ton SAF en 35.000 ton bijproducten. De bouw is gestart in 2026 en de eerste productie staat gepland voor 2028. Het project omvat de fabriek zelf, bijbehorende leidingen en tijdelijke werkterreinen. Je draagt direct bij aan de realisatie van een nieuwe industriële fabriek en de verduurzaming van de luchtvaart.

title: Hoofdmonteur Warmtepompen
description: Bij DeWarmte maken we slimme en betaalbare warmtepompen waarmee we woningen van het gas af helpen. We ontwerpen onze producten zelf, assembleren ze in Utrecht en zorgen samen met onze installatiepartners dat ze bij steeds meer mensen thuis komen te staan. We groeien hard. Tot nu toe worden al onze warmtepompen geïnstalleerd door externe partners, maar daar komt verandering in. We gaan onze eigen installatieteams opbouwen en zoeken daarom een Hoofdmonteur Warmtepompen die hierin het voortouw neemt. Je bent een ervaren monteur die graag zelf de handen uit de mouwen steekt, maar ook energie krijgt van het begeleiden van anderen. Je gaat samen met je team op pad, bent verantwoordelijk voor de kwaliteit van de installaties en helpt ons om steeds meer monteurs op te leiden. Je komt dus niet in een bestaand team terecht. Je helpt het team zelf opbouwen. Wat ga je doen? Als Hoofdmonteur ben je verantwoordelijk voor de installatie van onze warmtepompen bij klanten thuis. Je begint met het leiden van ons eerste interne installatieteam en helpt ons om de komende jaren onze eigen installatiecapaciteit verder uit te bouwen. Je installeert warmtepompen en leidt je team Je gaat samen met een collega-monteur op pad om onze warmtepompen bij klanten thuis te installeren. Je bent verantwoordelijk voor de volledige installatie, van de technische uitvoering en het oplossen van onverwachte problemen tot de oplevering. Je zorgt dat installaties veilig, efficiënt en volgens onze kwaliteitsstandaarden worden uitgevoerd. Je bent het aanspreekpunt voor de klant tijdens de installatie. Je legt uit wat jullie doen, beantwoordt vragen en zorgt dat de klant met een goed gevoel achterblijft. Je stemt waar nodig af met onze werkvoorbereiders en collega's op kantoor over planning, materialen en technische uitdagingen. Je bouwt mee aan ons interne installatieteam Je begeleidt en traint nieuwe monteurs en helpt hen om zelfstandig installaties uit te kunnen voeren. Je denkt mee over het aannemen van nieuwe collega's en hoe we ons installatieteam verder kunnen uitbreiden. Je helpt onze installatiestandaarden en werkwijzen verder te ontwikkelen. Je signaleert wat er in de praktijk beter of slimmer kan en neemt initiatief om dit te verbeteren. Je deelt feedback vanuit het veld met onze engineers, werkvoorbereiders en productontwikkelaars, zodat we onze producten en installaties continu kunnen verbeteren. Wie zoeken wij? We zoeken iemand die zijn vak goed verstaat, verantwoordelijkheid neemt en het leuk vindt om anderen beter te maken. Je hoeft niet eerder een heel team te hebben opgebouwd, maar je moet wel zin hebben om die uitdaging aan te gaan. Je hebt ruime ervaring met het installeren van warmtepompen, cv-installaties of andere verwarmingssystemen. Ervaring met warmtepompen heeft een sterke voorkeur. Je hebt een goede technische basis in installatietechniek, elektrotechniek en/of werktuigbouwkunde. Je kunt zelfstandig installaties uitvoeren, technische tekeningen lezen en onverwachte problemen oplossen. Je hebt ervaring met het begeleiden van andere monteurs, of bent klaar om die verantwoordelijkheid op je te nemen. Je werkt nauwkeurig en veilig en vindt het belangrijk om goed werk af te leveren. Je communiceert makkelijk met klanten en collega's en kunt technische zaken begrijpelijk uitleggen. Je neemt initiatief, denkt in oplossingen en voelt je verantwoordelijk voor het eindresultaat. Je spreekt goed Nederlands en hebt rijbewijs B. Een relevante mbo-opleiding en certificeringen zoals VCA, NEN 3140 of CO-vakmanschap zijn mooi meegenomen. Heb je nog niet alle benodigde certificaten? Dan kijken we samen wat je nog kunt behalen. Wat bieden wij jou? Een salaris van €4.000 tot €6.000 bruto per maand op basis van 40 uur, afhankelijk van je ervaring. Een sleutelrol in ons bedrijf: je wordt de eerste Hoofdmonteur van ons interne installatieteam en helpt dit verder uit te bouwen. Veel vrijheid en verantwoordelijkheid: je krijgt de ruimte om mee te denken over hoe we installeren, samenwerken en nieuwe monteurs opleiden. Goed materiaal: een volledig uitgeruste werkbus en professioneel gereedschap. 26 vakantiedagen en 13 ADV-dagen op basis van 40 uur, met de mogelijkheid om te kiezen voor een hogere beloning in plaats van ADV. Een goede pensioenregeling volgens de cao Metaal & Techniek. Mogelijkheden om jezelf verder te ontwikkelen, zowel technisch als in het begeleiden en aansturen van een team. Een betrokken team met korte lijnen, weinig bureaucratie en regelmatig leuke activiteiten, van borrels en teamuitjes tot onze jaarlijkse wintersport. Waarom DeWarmte? Bij DeWarmte geloven we dat verduurzaming pas echt werkt als het voor iedereen bereikbaar en aantrekkelijk is. Daarom ontwikkelen we slimme, betaalbare warmtepompen die we zelf ontwerpen en assembleren. We zijn een groeiend bedrijf waar veel gebeurt en waar je echt invloed hebt op hoe we dingen aanpakken. We houden van mensen die initiatief nemen, samenwerken en niet wachten tot iemand anders een probleem oplost. Als Hoofdmonteur krijg je de kans om vanaf het begin mee te bouwen aan onze eigen installatieorganisatie. Je werkt zelf aan mooie technische installaties, leidt nieuwe monteurs op en helpt bepalen hoe we dit in de toekomst op grotere schaal gaan doen. Klaar om samen met ons iets op te bouwen? Solliciteer en kom kennismaken. We vertellen je graag meer over DeWarmte, onze warmtepompen en onze plannen voor het interne installatieteam. Compensation: €4K – €6K per month • €4K – €6K per month Find Jobs in Netherlands on Arbeitnow

Je bouwt mee aan ons interne installatieteam

  • Je begeleidt en traint nieuwe monteurs en helpt hen om zelfstandig installaties uit te kunnen voeren.

Wie zoeken wij?

We zoeken iemand die zijn vak goed verstaat, verantwoordelijkheid neemt en het leuk vindt om anderen beter te maken. Je hoeft niet eerder een heel team te hebben opgebouwd, maar je moet wel zin hebben om die uitdaging aan te gaan.

  • Je hebt ruime ervaring met het installeren van warmtepompen, cv-installaties of andere verwarmingssystemen. Ervaring met warmtepompen heeft een sterke voorkeur.

  • Je hebt een goede technische basis in installatietechniek, elektrotechniek en/of werktuigbouwkunde.

  • Je kunt zelfstandig installaties uitvoeren, technische tekeningen lezen en onverwachte problemen oplossen.

  • Je hebt ervaring met het begeleiden van andere monteurs, of bent klaar om die verantwoordelijkheid op je te nemen.

  • Je werkt nauwkeurig en veilig en vindt het belangrijk om goed werk af te leveren.

  • Je neemt initiatief, denkt in oplossingen en voelt je verantwoordelijk voor het eindresultaat.

Wat bieden wij jou?

Waarom DeWarmte?

Bij DeWarmte geloven we dat verduurzaming pas echt werkt als het voor iedereen bereikbaar en aantrekkelijk is. Daarom ontwikkelen we slimme, betaalbare warmtepompen die we zelf ontwerpen en assembleren.

Als Hoofdmonteur krijg je de kans om vanaf het begin mee te bouwen aan onze eigen installatieorganisatie. Je werkt zelf aan mooie technische installaties, leidt nieuwe monteurs op en helpt bepalen hoe we dit in de toekomst op grotere schaal gaan doen.

Solliciteer en kom kennismaken. We vertellen je graag meer over DeWarmte, onze warmtepompen en onze plannen voor het interne installatieteam.

Wat bieden wij Binnen het Data & AI Office krijg je een veelzijdige functie waarin je direct samenwerkt met de business en zichtbaar bijdraagt aan de ontwikkeling van Univé. Voor complexere analyses gebruik je Python. Daarnaast maak je gebruik van ChatGPT en andere moderne data- en AI-toepassingen; Innovatie en autonomie: je krijgt ruimte om nieuwe technieken te onderzoeken en eigen ideeën te ontwikkelen, testen en verbeteren; Hybride werken: je werkt gemiddeld 50% op kantoor en 50% vanuit huis, inclusief ondersteuning voor je thuiswerkplek; Extra voordelen: korting op je schade- en zorgverzekeringen bij Univé. We ontwikkelen het centrale datafundament, bouwen betrouwbare dataproducten en zetten data en AI in om besluitvorming, processen en klantbediening te verbeteren. Je komt terecht in een omgeving met data scientists, data engineers, data-analisten, business informatie analisten en andere dataspecialisten. Samen met collega’s uit de waardestromen en bedrijfsonderdelen brengen we kennis van data, technologie en de business bij elkaar. We geloven in eigenaarschap, vakmanschap en samenwerking. We experimenteren graag, maar zorgen er ook voor dat succesvolle oplossingen veilig, betrouwbaar en beheersbaar in productie worden genomen. title: Senior Customer Success Manager
description: Heel werkend Nederland op de fiets! Dat is de krachtige missie van Lease a Bike, waar we ons dagelijks vol passie voor inzetten. Om onze marktleidende positie verder uit te bouwen en nog meer impact te maken, zijn wij op zoek naar een commercieel gedreven Senior Customer Success Manager. In deze rol krijg jij de verantwoordelijkheid over een portfolio van middelgrote en grote accounts. Je helpt nieuwe klanten succesvol te onboarden en bouwt aan langetermijnrelaties. Een hoge klanttevredenheid en zo veel mogelijk werknemers op de fiets krijgen zijn hierbij jouw belangrijkste doelen. Dit doe je natuurlijk niet alleen: je werkt nauw samen in een gedreven team van 6 collega’s. Jouw rol als Customer Success Manager Als Customer Success Manager ben jij de centrale spil tussen jouw klanten en onze interne organisatie. Je schakelt dagelijks met werkgevers en bent intern de verbindende schakel tussen Sales, Product & Innovation, Marketing en Customer Support. In jouw portefeuille richt jij je specifiek op bedrijven met 500+ medewerkers. Zodra Sales de samenwerkingsovereenkomst heeft getekend, neem jij het stokje over. Je leidt de implementatie en begeleidt de klant gedurende de gehele levenscyclus. Je adviseert werkgevers bij cruciale beleidskeuzes, helpt hen het platform optimaal in te richten en ontwikkelt gerichte activatiecampagnes. Zo zorg je ervoor dat de fietsregeling ook op de lange termijn top-of-mind blijft en de betrokkenheid van werknemers continu hoog is, met als ultiem doel: zoveel mogelijk werknemers op de fiets krijgen! Daarnaast ben je analytisch ijzersterk. Je gebruikt data om jouw klantsegment grondig te analyseren, ontdekt waar kansen liggen en weet creatieve ideeën om te zetten in concrete acties en resultaat. Wat vragen we van jou? Een afgeronde hbo- of wo-opleiding; Minimaal 3 jaar relevante werkervaring in Customer Success of Accountmanagement; Aantoonbare ervaring met het begeleiden van implementatietrajecten, relatiebeheer en het schrijven van accountplannen; Commercieel ingesteld en communicatief ijzersterk: je doorgrondt klantbehoeften snel en vertaalt deze naar effectieve actieplannen; Een hoge mate van zelfstandigheid en het vermogen om projecten met diverse stakeholders of complexe vraagstukken te leiden; Een sterk probleemoplossend en analytisch vermogen met focus op het uitbouwen van duurzame klantrelaties; Je kunt goed plannen, bewaart het overzicht en gaat gestructureerd te werk; Een flexibele en hands-on mentaliteit die past bij een snelgroeiende marktleider; Uitstekende beheersing van de Nederlandse en Engelse taal in woord en schrift; Wat bieden wij?  Naast een uitdagende rol met veel vrijheid, verantwoordelijkheid en een grote impact op de verdere groei van Lease a Bike bieden wij nog veel meer: Een bruto maandsalaris tussen de € 3.950,- en € 4.450.  8% vakantiegeld, een bonusregeling van 10% én een jaarlijkse winstuitkering; Een jaarlijkse toekenning van 20 wettelijke verlofdagen, 5 bovenwettelijke vakantiedagen en 6 ATV-dagen op basis van een fulltime dienstverband; Een gloednieuwe leasefiets naar keuze (Pon-merk) met een maandelijkse werkgeversbijdrage; Een reiskostenvergoeding of Shuttel-kaart voor de dagen dat je naar kantoor reist; Focus op ontwikkeling: De mogelijkheid om je continu te blijven ontwikkelen via onder andere onze Winter- en Summerlabstrainingen; Een gezonde lunch op kantoor in Amersfoort tegen een kleine bijdrage; Een thuiswerkplek door ons gefaciliteerd met de mogelijkheid voor een netto thuiswerkvergoeding voor als je af en toe thuis wil werken; Een collectieve Zorgverzekering bij ONVZ of Zilveren Kruis met een werkgeversbijdrage; Én, last but not least, een aantrekkelijke pensioenregeling bij het Pon Pensioenfonds van 30% waarbij Lease a Bike 20% bijdraagt. Over de organisatie Lease a Bike is ontstaan vanuit liefde voor mensen en fietsen. Voor ons is fietsen niet zomaar een manier van vervoer. Voor ons is fietsen een ‘way of life’. Fietsen is goed voor je gezondheid. Goed voor je portemonnee. Goed voor de wereld. Anderen stimuleren om de fiets te pakken, daar gaan wij voor! Wil jij een bijdrage leveren aan een duurzamere wereld, waarbij vitaliteit en fun hand in hand gaan? Join the ride en draag bij aan de verwezenlijking van onze missie. Als scale-up is Lease a Bike onderdeel van mobiliteitsprovider Bike Mobility Services Group (Pon)!
